project.name: Screen — 39.4862,-75.0257
project.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)

headline: 2% probability this project energizes on its announced schedule.

probability.model: The air permit is treated as the critical path. Months available is the target energization date minus today. Months required is the pre-application preparation period plus the pathway's likely duration for that state agency. The pathway's own optimistic-to-pessimistic spread is read as roughly plus or minus two standard deviations, so sigma = (high - low) / 4, floored at one month. The probability is the normal CDF of slack over sigma, clipped to [0.02, 0.97] because nothing here justifies claiming certainty. Hard stops are a hard cap at 0.05: a moratorium, an unavailable offset market or a consumed increment is not a schedule risk, it is a different outcome. Turbine delivery, construction and interconnection are not modelled — they are separate constraints and each is documented as binding on its own.
basis: 16 months to the announced date. 3 months to prepare a complete application plus 66 months of agency review = 69 months required.
Slack -53 months against a sigma of 15.7 months, taken from the 41-104 month range for Major nonattainment NSR.

emissions.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)

basis.emission_factors: AP-42 Table 3.1-1 / 3.1-2a / 3.1-3, uncontrolled natural gas turbine > 3 MW
basis.heat_rate: 10,500 Btu/kWh HHV (module default for this prime mover)
basis.heat_input: 400 MW x 1000 kW/MW x 10,500 Btu/kWh / 1e6 = 4,200 MMBtu/hr
basis.hours_basis: 8,760 hr/yr — no enforceable cap, so PTE is computed at full-time operation regardless of intended dispatch
basis.method: PTE (tpy) = EF (lb/MMBtu) x heat input (MMBtu/hr) x hours (hr/yr) / 2000

pathway.label: Major nonattainment NSR

source_category.reasoning: Simple cycle, no steam cycle, so not a 'steam electric plant' and no boiler. Not a listed category despite 4,200 MMBtu/hr of heat input. Major source threshold is 250 tpy. Worth confirming with the state — a few agencies read the boiler entry more broadly than EPA does.
source_category.citation: 40 CFR 52.21(b)(1)(i)(a); the 'List of 28' named source categories

triggers_fired.name: nonattainment_designation
triggers_fired.detail: Cumberland County, NJ is designated nonattainment for: ozone (serious, Philadelphia-Atlantic City, PA-NJ); ozone (marginal, Philadelphia-Atlantic City, PA-NJ).

triggers_fired.name: major_nonattainment_nsr
triggers_fired.detail: NOx PTE of 5,887 tpy is over the 50 tpy major threshold for a serious ozone nonattainment area. Requires LAER (no cost defense, unlike BACT) and 1.20:1 emission offsets — 7,064 tons of verified reductions bought from existing sources in the area.

triggers_fired.name: title_v
triggers_fired.detail: Title V operating permit required — criteria pollutant PTE 5,887 tpy over 100 tpy. Runs after the construction permit; usually does not block construction but does add annual compliance cost and a public comment window of its own.

triggers_fired.name: nsps_turbine
triggers_fired.detail: NSPS Subpart KKKK applies, and EPA's 15 January 2026 rule (91 Fed. Reg. 1910) added Subpart KKKKa. That rule did not settle the trailer-mounted question, and it did not settle it in the direction most coverage claims. It finalised a conditional exclusion removing turbines from the 'stationary combustion turbine' definition where the unit qualifies as a nonroad engine and is certified under Title II. The exclusion is not operative: it takes effect only if EPA adopts Title II standards for portable turbines, a separate rulemaking that has not happened. Meanwhile the NAACP is asking a federal court in Mississippi to shut down 27 unpermitted turbines at xAI's Colossus 2, with a preliminary injunction hearing set for late August 2026. Underwriting a trailer-mounted fast path today means underwriting an open legal question, not a loophole.
triggers_fired.citation: 40 CFR 60 Subpart KKKK and new Subpart KKKKa; 91 Fed. Reg. 1910 (15 Jan 2026); NAACP v. xAI (N.D. Miss.), PI hearing late Aug 2026

triggers_fired.name: state_toxics
triggers_fired.detail: NJ runs a state air toxics program on top of the federal HAP rules. Expect a separate modeling demonstration for formaldehyde and, for engines, acrolein. This often drives stack height more than the NAAQS analysis does.
triggers_fired.citation: NJ DEP EJ Law N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157, effective April 2023

triggers_fired.name: ozone_transport_region
triggers_fired.detail: NJ is in the Ozone Transport Region. NOx is subject to nonattainment-style requirements statewide regardless of local monitor data, and the major source threshold for VOC/NOx is 50 tpy.

triggers_fired.name: ej_denial_authority
triggers_fired.detail: NJ gives the agency authority to deny a permit outright in an overburdened community, independent of whether the emissions modeling passes. This is a discretionary denial risk, not a timeline risk.
triggers_fired.citation: NJ DEP EJ Law N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157, effective April 2023

alternate_sites.delta_statement: Move 37 miles SSW to Kent County, DE. Major PSD instead of Major nonattainment NSR. Save ~39 months.
notes: DE is not one of the states modelled in detail, so its timeline is the federal default and its state-specific triggers (toxics programs, transport region, EJ statutes) are not evaluated. Some of the apparent gain may be that gap rather than a real difference. Confirm with the state agency before optioning land on it.

options.label: Switch to solid oxide fuel cells
options.config: 400 MW fuel_cell on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: Solid oxide fuel cells emit almost no criteria pollutants, which usually takes the air permit off the critical path entirely. CO2 is not solved — they still burn gas. Much higher capital cost per MW, a supplier list you can count on one hand, and lead times that are themselves the constraint at data center scale.

options.label: Add SCR
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (scr), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: SCR is the standard NOx answer and it is also the expensive one: catalyst, reactor volume in the exhaust path, and an ammonia or urea storage and handling system on site, which brings its own safety review and often its own local permit. Small heat-rate penalty from the pressure drop. It does nothing for CO.

options.label: Add oxidation catalyst
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (oxidation_catalyst), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: An oxidation catalyst cuts CO by about 90% and VOC by about half. No reagent, no storage tank, small pressure drop, and it is cheap next to SCR. Worth checking first whenever CO is the pollutant sitting over the threshold — on an uncontrolled turbine that is more often the case than people expect.

options.label: Add SCR + oxidation catalyst
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (scr, oxidation_catalyst), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: SCR is the standard NOx answer and it is also the expensive one: catalyst, reactor volume in the exhaust path, and an ammonia or urea storage and handling system on site, which brings its own safety review and often its own local permit. Small heat-rate penalty from the pressure drop. It does nothing for CO. An oxidation catalyst cuts CO by about 90% and VOC by about half. No reagent, no storage tank, small pressure drop, and it is cheap next to SCR. Worth checking first whenever CO is the pollutant sitting over the threshold — on an uncontrolled turbine that is more often the case than people expect.

options.label: Add dry low-NOx combustors
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (dry_low_nox), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: Dry low-NOx combustors are a turbine specification, not an add-on: you order the machine that way. No reagent and no aftertreatment, but the reduction is smaller than SCR and there are turndown and CO trade-offs at part load.

options.label: Switch simple cycle to combined cycle
options.config: 400 MW combined_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: Combined cycle burns roughly two thirds the fuel per MWh, so tons per year drop with no control equipment at all. The catch is legal, not thermal: the HRSG and steam turbine make the plant a 'fossil fuel-fired steam electric plant' over 250 MMBtu/hr, which drops the PSD major threshold from 250 tpy to 100 tpy. Check both directions before assuming it helps. Also adds water, a longer build, and a second machine in an order book already full.

options.label: Combined cycle + SCR + oxidation catalyst
options.config: 400 MW combined_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (scr, oxidation_catalyst), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: Combined cycle burns roughly two thirds the fuel per MWh, so tons per year drop with no control equipment at all. The catch is legal, not thermal: the HRSG and steam turbine make the plant a 'fossil fuel-fired steam electric plant' over 250 MMBtu/hr, which drops the PSD major threshold from 250 tpy to 100 tpy. Check both directions before assuming it helps. Also adds water, a longer build, and a second machine in an order book already full. SCR is the standard NOx answer and it is also the expensive one: catalyst, reactor volume in the exhaust path, and an ammonia or urea storage and handling system on site, which brings its own safety review and often its own local permit. Small heat-rate penalty from the pressure drop. It does nothing for CO.

options.label: Split into two separate sources
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760), split into 2 units
options.cost_note: Splitting the plant only works if the pieces are genuinely separate stationary sources. Units serving one campus, under one owner, will be aggregated. Treat this as a conversation with the agency, not a design decision.
warnings: Aggregation risk. EPA will almost certainly treat one campus as one source.

best.label: Switch to solid oxide fuel cells
best.config: 400 MW fuel_cell on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
best.cost_note: Solid oxide fuel cells emit almost no criteria pollutants, which usually takes the air permit off the critical path entirely. CO2 is not solved — they still burn gas. Much higher capital cost per MW, a supplier list you can count on one hand, and lead times that are themselves the constraint at data center scale.

notes: Accept a run-hour cap (as designed): Holding NOx under 50 tpy would need a cap of 67 hr/yr (1% availability). That is not a data center power plant, it is a peaker.
Accept a run-hour cap, with SCR and oxidation catalyst: Holding NOx under 50 tpy would need a cap of 670 hr/yr (8% availability). That is not a data center power plant, it is a peaker.

Terrain relief decides whether it is a flat-site run or a complex-terrain run with terrain-following receptors, and complex terrain usually forces a taller stack.; land_cover: AERMET needs surface roughness, albedo and Bowen ratio from land cover to build the meteorological inputs for that AERMOD run.; points_of_interest: Schools, hospitals and residential parcels near the fenceline are both modelling receptors and the opposition map. Engines and major sources need both.; demographics: State has environmental-justice denial authority. Population and EJ indicators within radius decide whether this is a modelling exercise or a discretionary denial risk.; grid_interconnect: Over 200 MW or grid-tied. The interconnect study runs in parallel with the air permit and is frequently the longer pole.

steps.title: Run the decision tree
steps.why: Source category, then threshold, then PTE against threshold, then the overlays that add months.

steps.title: Source category
steps.why: Simple cycle, no steam cycle, so not a 'steam electric plant' and no boiler. Not a listed category despite 4,200 MMBtu/hr of heat input. Major source threshold is 250 tpy. Worth confirming with the state — a few agencies read the boiler entry more broadly than EPA does.
steps.citation: 40 CFR 52.21(b)(1)(i)(a); the 'List of 28' named source categories

steps.title: Applicable major-source threshold
steps.why: 250 tpy — not a listed category
steps.citation: 40 CFR 52.21(b)(1)(i)(a); the 'List of 28' named source categories

steps.title: Potential to emit vs threshold
steps.why: NOx at 5,887 tpy against 50 tpy. 8,760 hr/yr — no enforceable cap, so PTE is computed at full-time operation regardless of intended dispatch

steps.title: Nonattainment Designation
steps.why: FIRED — Cumberland County, NJ is designated nonattainment for: ozone (serious, Philadelphia-Atlantic City, PA-NJ); ozone (marginal, Philadelphia-Atlantic City, PA-NJ).

steps.title: Major Nonattainment Nsr
steps.why: FIRED — NOx PTE of 5,887 tpy is over the 50 tpy major threshold for a serious ozone nonattainment area. Requires LAER (no cost defense, unlike BACT) and 1.20:1 emission offsets — 7,064 tons of verified reductions bought from existing sources in the area.

steps.title: Class I Aqrv
steps.why: clear — No Class I area within screening range.

steps.title: Title V
steps.why: FIRED — Title V operating permit required — criteria pollutant PTE 5,887 tpy over 100 tpy. Runs after the construction permit; usually does not block construction but does add annual compliance cost and a public comment window of its own.

steps.title: State Toxics
steps.why: FIRED — NJ runs a state air toxics program on top of the federal HAP rules. Expect a separate modeling demonstration for formaldehyde and, for engines, acrolein. This often drives stack height more than the NAAQS analysis does.
steps.citation: NJ DEP EJ Law N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157, effective April 2023

steps.title: Ozone Transport Region
steps.why: FIRED — NJ is in the Ozone Transport Region. NOx is subject to nonattainment-style requirements statewide regardless of local monitor data, and the major source threshold for VOC/NOx is 50 tpy.

steps.title: Ej Denial Authority
steps.why: FIRED — NJ gives the agency authority to deny a permit outright in an overburdened community, independent of whether the emissions modeling passes. This is a discretionary denial risk, not a timeline risk.
steps.citation: NJ DEP EJ Law N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157, effective April 2023

steps.title: Pathway
steps.why: Major nonattainment NSR: 41-104 months (likely 66)

steps.title: Config search at this parcel
steps.why: Before moving the project, find out whether the equipment can move the pathway. Free, and controls are cheaper than land.

steps.title: Switch to solid oxide fuel cells
steps.why: Solid oxide fuel cells emit almost no criteria pollutants, which usually takes the air permit off the critical path entirely. CO2 is not solved — they still burn gas. Much higher capital cost per MW, a supplier list you can count on one hand, and lead times that are themselves the constraint at data center scale.

options.label: Switch to solid oxide fuel cells
options.config: 400 MW fuel_cell on natural_gas (uncontrolled), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: Solid oxide fuel cells emit almost no criteria pollutants, which usually takes the air permit off the critical path entirely. CO2 is not solved — they still burn gas. Much higher capital cost per MW, a supplier list you can count on one hand, and lead times that are themselves the constraint at data center scale.

options.label: Add SCR
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (scr), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: SCR is the standard NOx answer and it is also the expensive one: catalyst, reactor volume in the exhaust path, and an ammonia or urea storage and handling system on site, which brings its own safety review and often its own local permit. Small heat-rate penalty from the pressure drop. It does nothing for CO.

options.label: Add oxidation catalyst
options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (oxidation_catalyst), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)
options.cost_note: An oxidation catalyst cuts CO by about 90% and VOC by about half. No reagent, no storage tank, small pressure drop, and it is cheap next to SCR. Worth checking first whenever CO is the pollutant sitting over the threshold — on an uncontrolled turbine that is more often the case than people expect.

options.config: 400 MW simple_cycle_turbine on natural_gas (scr, oxidation_catalyst), no enforceable hour cap (PTE at 8760)

No reagent, no storage tank, small pressure drop, and it is cheap next to SCR. Worth checking first whenever CO is the pollutant sitting over the threshold — on an uncontrolled turbine that is more often the case than people expect.

steps.conclusion: Switch to solid oxide fuel cells: Major nonattainment NSR -> Minor NSR construction permit, ~44 months, 100% availability.

steps.title: Alternate-site search
steps.why: Major nonattainment NSR at the announced parcel. The permit you need is decided by where the land is, so search outward across county and state lines for ground where the same plant gets a faster answer.
